activeMisconceptions.title: Missing Base Case in Recursion
activeMisconceptions.studentReasoning: I thought the recursion would automatically stop when n became negative because there's no math left to do.
activeMisconceptions.explanation: Recursion has no 'automatic' awareness of mathematical intent. Unless you explicitly code an exit condition (e.g., `if (n <= 1) return 1;`), the Java Virtual Machine keeps pushing new activation frames onto the call stack until memory is exhausted (StackOverflowError).

activeMisconceptions.title: Array Index Out of Bounds (Length vs Last Index)
activeMisconceptions.studentReasoning: If an array has size 5, array[5] should be the 5th element.
activeMisconceptions.explanation: Java arrays are 0-indexed. An array of size N stores items from index `0` up to index `N - 1`. Attempting to read `array[array.length]` always throws an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

counterExample.incorrectCode:
int[] arr = new int[5];
System.out.println(arr[5]); // Crash! Valid indices are 0,1,2,3,4
counterExample.correctCode:
int[] arr = new int[5];
System.out.println(arr[arr.length - 1]); // Last element!
counterExample.trace: Length = 5. Indices: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]. index 5 does not exist.

spacedRepetitionQueue.title: Recursion: Base Case Invariant
spacedRepetitionQueue.prompt: Why must a recursive function always have a base case?
spacedRepetitionQueue.answer: To provide a terminating condition that halts further recursive calls, unwinds the call stack, and prevents StackOverflowError.
